tldr: AWS grew 39% to $46.0B, its fastest in nearly five years, but Amazon missed on EPS and shares fell roughly 5-11% after hours as the ~$220B 2026 capex plan pushed free cash flow sharply lower.
Intel's Q3 revenue rose 21% to $16.5B, but a Q4 guide of $15-16B sent shares down about 17% after hours; Sandisk beat with $11.0B revenue, guided Q2 to $12.2-12.6B and announced an 8-for-1 split.
Banks shelved a $5-7B bond sale for an Anthropic-tied Texas data center as the state's grid review freezes new projects, while Korean chip startup FuriosaAI raised $620M at a $2.9B valuation.

items.title: AWS grows 39% to $46B, fastest in nearly five years, but Amazon misses on EPS and revenue and shares fall after hours
items.summary: Amazon's Q3 net sales rose 12% to $201.9B and operating income was $28.1B. AWS sales grew 39% to $46.0B with $17.8B operating income. EPS of $1.89 missed the roughly $1.97 consensus, and trailing free cash flow turned deeply negative. Amazon held its 2026 capex plan near $220B, and shares fell roughly 5-11% in extended trading depending on the time of measurement.
items.why_it_matters: The strongest cloud acceleration in years, with capacity still tight, validates the AI infrastructure spend. The cash burn and the market's reaction show how little tolerance investors have for capex that outruns free cash flow.

items.title: Intel beats Q3 on AI data-center strength but guides Q4 well below consensus; shares drop about 17% after hours
items.summary: Intel reported Q3 2026 revenue of $16.5B (up 21% YoY), non-GAAP EPS of $0.52 and GAAP EPS of $0.60, with GAAP gross margin 43.0%. It guided Q4 revenue to $15.0-16.0B and non-GAAP EPS to $0.25, well under Street expectations. Management pointed to PC weakness and supply constraints; coverage also cites an Israel plant incident.
items.why_it_matters: A guide-down from the main US foundry bet, driven by PC demand hit by memory prices, shows the AI memory squeeze spilling into client compute. It also puts pressure on the 14A and 18A funding story.

items.title: Sandisk posts $11.0B quarter above guidance, guides next quarter to $12.2-12.6B and announces 8-for-1 split
items.summary: Sandisk's fiscal Q1 2027 revenue was $11.0B, up 23% sequentially and above its $10.3-10.8B guide, with non-GAAP EPS of $49.51 versus a $44-46 guide. It guided fiscal Q2 revenue to $12.2-12.6B and non-GAAP EPS (pre-split) to $55-57. It repurchased about $5.0B of stock in the quarter and announced an eight-for-one forward split effective Nov 19, 2026.
items.why_it_matters: NAND pricing is following DRAM into a data-center-driven upcycle, with margins around 85% on the company's figures. The guide still implies sequential growth slowing to low teens.

items.title: Banks shelve bond sale for Anthropic-tied Texas data center as state grid review freezes new projects
items.summary: Bloomberg reports that banks have shelved a planned high-yield bond sale, reportedly $5-7B, meant to refinance part of a roughly $15B loan for the Nexus Data Centers campus in Hubbard, Texas, leased to Anthropic and backed by Google. Secondary coverage ties the delay to Gov. Greg Abbott's hold on new data-center approvals while ERCOT and state agencies audit grid risk. Sales may be staggered over the next year, leaving lenders holding the debt.
items.why_it_matters: It is a concrete case of data-center policy risk reaching project finance for a frontier lab's compute, days after Anthropic's S-1 flagged moratoriums as a top risk. Banks holding the loan longer also tests appetite for AI-linked junk debt.
key_numbers: Texas review reportedly runs to mid-December

items.title: Korean AI-chip startup FuriosaAI raises $620M Series D at $2.9B valuation, about four times its last
items.summary: FuriosaAI says it closed a $620M Series D at a $2.9B post-money valuation, roughly 4x its prior $735M valuation. Reports name Korea's National Growth Fund (about $280M with Infinitum Partners, per one account) and Cisco Investments among backers. items.why_it_matters: State-backed capital is funding a non-Nvidia inference alternative in Korea. The valuation jump is a sign that investor interest in inference silicon is widening beyond the US.

learn.title: Read free cash flow as OCF minus capex, and size the funding runway
learn.why_today: The item reports AWS growth of 39% alongside a ~$220B capex plan and sharply lower trailing free cash flow, which is the OCF-versus-capex squeeze in practice.
learn.explanation: Free cash flow is operating cash flow minus capital expenditure; it is what remains to repay debt, buy back stock or pay dividends. When capex outgrows operating cash flow, FCF turns negative and the gap must be funded by cash on hand, debt or equity. Trailing-twelve-month FCF lags capex ramps because spending hits immediately while the revenue it enables arrives later, so a growth segment can look strong while FCF falls. A simple runway model compounds debt at an interest rate and adds the annual shortfall. It breaks when OCF grows, capex is leased or off-balance-sheet, or timing of payables distorts a single year. The numbers below are illustrative, not Amazon's.
learn.python:
# Illustrative numbers only (not Amazon's actual figures), in $B per year.
ocf = 140.0          # operating cash flow
capex = 220.0        # capital expenditure
fcf = ocf - capex
print("FCF:", fcf)
# Capex funded by debt: how many years of negative FCF before net debt reaches a limit?
debt, limit, rate = 0.0, 300.0, 0.05
for year in range(1, 11):
    debt = debt * (1 + rate) - fcf
    print(year, round(debt, 1))
    if debt > limit:
        print("limit hit in year", year); break
